label: Garland single-mode passive fibre TAP 100M-100G (OS2501)
description: Garland OS2501 passive single-mode fibre TAP - one tap, 50/50 split, 1310/1550 nm over OS2 9 um LC single-mode fibre, passing 100M/1G/10G/25G/40G/100G unpowered with copies on two monitor ports. No power source, no IP or MAC address.
notes: Garland's own fibre-TAP table gives one row per part number, and the OS2501 row is: '**TAPs 1; TAP Media OS2 9 um SMF; Monitor Media OS2 9 um SMF; Speed 100M / 1G / 10G / 25G / 40G / 100G; Wavelength 1310 / 1550 nm; Connector LC; Split ratio 50/50**'. **Four LC ports, two network and two monitor** - the same shape as the OM4501 multimode sibling already in this catalogue (and as the OM3501 and P10GSFPA cage variants), because a '1 TAP' duplex fibre unit inline between two devices needs two network ports and each direction's 50/50 copy needs a monitor port. That is geometry rather than a guess, and it is the reason this model can be trusted where a copper TAP's port list could not. **The speed ladder is the whole row, not the headline:** 100M through 100G, which is why `speedCaps` runs `[100, 1000, 10000, 25000, 40000, 100000]` rather than stopping at the 10G that most OS2 taps do. 1310/1550 nm, 50/50 with other ratios orderable. **Nothing to configure and no power:** a passive optical split keeps the live link up even when the monitoring tool is unplugged, so there is no `poeIn`, no address and no capabilities. The -W variants in the same table (OS2501W) go to 400G over a wider 1270-1310/1510-1590 nm window and are a separate part, not this one.
